title: İnsanlar ve yerler
canDo: İnsanları, nesneleri ve yerleri who, which, that, where ve whose ile tanımlayabilir, bilmediğim bir kelimeyi açıklayarak anlatabilir ve sevdiğim bir yeri ayrıntılı bir şekilde tanıtabilirim.

lessons.title: Kim? Hangisi?
lessons.goal: who ve which ile insanları ve nesneleri tanımlayabilirim.

learn.explanation:
**İlgi cümleleri (relative clauses)**, hangi kişiden ya da şeyden bahsettiğimizi **tanımlar**. İki cümleyi birleştirir.

| İlgi zamiri | Ne için? | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **who** | **insanlar** | The woman **who** organised the wedding is my aunt. |
| **which** | **nesneler, hayvanlar** | He made the cake **which** everyone loved. |

**İki cümleyi birleştirmek:**

- The man is a chef. **He** is dancing. → The man **who** is dancing is a chef.
- I bought a phone. **It** has a great camera. → I bought a phone **which** has a great camera.

**Dikkat:** who / which, he / she / it'in **yerine** geçer. Tekrar etmeyin:

- The man who ~~he~~ is dancing...

Bu tür tanımlayıcı ilgi cümlelerinde **virgül kullanılmaz**.

examples.en: A pilot is a person who flies planes.
I've lost the keys which were on the table.
The people who live next door are very friendly.
examples.tr: Yan evde oturan insanlar çok cana yakın.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede ilgi cümlesi ismin önüne gelir ve ekle yapılır: "dans eden adam", "herkesin sevdiği pasta". İngilizcede sıralama tersine döner: isim önce, ilgi cümlesi sonra gelir: "the man who is dancing", "the cake which everyone loved". Türkçe sırayı korumaya çalışmak ("the dancing who man") en sık yapılan hatadır.

lessons.title: That ve atlama
lessons.goal: that kullanabilir, ilgi zamirini ne zaman atlayabileceğimi bilirim.

discover.title: Bir şehrin unutulmaz insanları
discover.body:
Every neighbourhood has people that everyone knows.

In our street, there's Hüseyin Bey, the shoe repairer. He's the man that fixes everything: shoes, bags, even suitcases. The shop he works in is tiny, but it's always busy.

Then there's Fatma Hanım, the woman who sells simit at the corner every morning. The simit she sells are the best in the city, and she knows everyone's name.

And there's Rıza, the cat that sleeps on the bakery window. He's the only cat I know that has his own Instagram account!

questions.prompt: What does Hüseyin Bey do?
Who is Rıza?
questions.explanation: "Rıza, the cat that sleeps on the bakery window"

learn.explanation:
**that**, tanımlayıcı ilgi cümlelerinde **who ve which yerine** kullanılabilir. Günlük konuşmada çok yaygındır.

- The man **that** (= who) fixes everything.
- The cat **that** (= which) sleeps on the window.

**İlgi zamirini atlamak:**

İlgi zamiri cümlenin **nesnesi** ise (ondan sonra **bir özne** geliyorsa) atlanabilir.

| Özne (atlanamaz) | Nesne (atlanabilir) |
|---|---|
| The woman **who sells** simit. | The simit (**that**) **she** sells. |
| The man **that fixes** shoes. | The shop (**which**) **he** works in. |
| who / that + **fiil** | (who / that) + **özne** + fiil |

- The book (that) **I** bought is great. ✓
- The book ~~bought~~... → The book **that** is on the table. (Burada that öznedir, atlanamaz.)

learn.explanation:
**where** → **yerler** için (-dığı yer)

- This is the street **where** I grew up. (Büyüdüğüm sokak)
- That's the bakery **where** we bought bread.

**where** = in which / at which. Ondan sonra **özne + fiil** gelir.

**Dikkat:** Yer bir **nesne** gibi kullanılıyorsa **which / that** gelir:

| where (orada bir şey olur) | which / that (yer özne ya da nesne) |
|---|---|
| The city **where** I live. | The city **which** has the best food. |
| The hotel **where** we stayed. | The hotel **that** we chose. |

**whose** → **sahiplik** (-in, -ın)

- That's the family **whose** son was my friend. (Oğlu benim arkadaşım olan aile)
- I have a friend **whose** father is a famous actor.

**whose + isim** birlikte kullanılır.

**Not:** Dinlediğiniz ve okuduğunuz metinlerde virgülle ayrılmış ilgi cümleleri de göreceksiniz: *My cousin, whose family owns a hotel, ...* Bunlar kişiyi tanımlamaz, sadece **ek bilgi** verir. Ayrıntılarını B2'de göreceğiz.

learn.explanation:
Bir kelimeyi bilmediğinizde **durmayın, tarif edin!** Bu, iyi konuşanların en önemli becerilerinden biridir.

| Ne? | Kalıp |
|---|---|
| Kişi | It's **a person who** ... / It's **someone who** ... |
| Nesne | It's **a thing which / that** ... / It's **something you use to / for** ... |
| Yer | It's **a place where** ... |
| Tür | It's **a kind of** ... / It's **a type of** ... |
| Benzerlik | It's **similar to** ... / It's **like** a ..., **but** ... |
| Görünüş | It's **made of** ... / It **looks like** ... |

**Yardım istemek:**

- **What's the word for** ...?
- **What do you call** a person who ...?
- **I don't know the word in English, but** ...
- **Do you know what I mean?**

**Karşı taraf:** Do you mean ...? / Oh, you mean a ...!

examples.en: What do you call a person who designs buildings?

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe konuşanlar İngilizce konuşurken bir kelimeyi bilmediklerinde genellikle duraklar ya da Türkçe kelimeyi söyler. Bunun yerine "It's a thing which..." ile tarif etmek hem iletişimi sürdürür hem de pratik yapmanızı sağlar. "What do you call...?" sorusu kelime öğrenmenin en kolay yollarından biridir.

lessons.title: Benim yerim
lessons.goal: Sevdiğim bir yeri ilgi cümleleri ve betimleyici kelimelerle canlı bir şekilde tanıtabilirim.

discover.title: Gezgin blogu: Saklı bir köy
discover.body:
Last spring I discovered a village that I'll never forget.

It's a small place in the mountains above Fethiye, where only about 200 people live. The road which goes up to the village is narrow and steep, but the view from the top is worth it.

The heart of the village is a little square with an old plane tree, where the men play backgammon and drink tea all day. Next to it, there's a café whose owner, Gülsüm Teyze, makes the best gözleme I've ever eaten.

What I loved most were the people. Strangers who I'd never met invited me into their homes. It's the kind of place that reminds you how kind people can be.

questions.prompt: How many people live in the village?
What does the writer say about the people?
options: They invited the writer into their homes.

learn.explanation:
**Bir yeri tanıtırken:**

| Bilgi | Kalıp |
|---|---|
| Genel | It's a **small / lively / peaceful** place **where** ... |
| Konum | It's **in the mountains / by the sea / near** ... |
| Öne çıkan | **The heart of** the town is ... / **The best thing about** it is ... |
| Kişiler | There's a café **whose owner** ... / The people **who live there** ... |
| Duygu | It's **the kind of place that** ... / It **reminds me of** ... |
| Tavsiye | It's **worth visiting**. / **If you go there**, don't miss ... |

**Betimleyici sıfatlar:**

| Olumlu | Olumsuz |
|---|---|
| peaceful, lively, charming, picturesque | crowded, noisy, dirty, touristy |

**Virgüllü ilgi cümleleri:** Yeri zaten belli olan bir şeye **ek bilgi** eklerken virgül kullanılır: *a village above Fethiye, where only 200 people live*. Bu kullanımda **that** kullanılmaz.

**İlgi cümleleriyle zenginleştirme:**

- There's a café. → There's **a tiny café whose owner** makes the best gözleme **I've ever eaten**.

task.prompt: Sevdiğiniz bir yeri (şehir, köy, semt, kafe, park) tanıtan bir blog yazısı yazın (130–160 kelime). En az 5 ilgi cümlesi (who, which, that, where, whose) ve en az 4 betimleyici sıfat kullanın. Sonunda okuyucuya bir tavsiye verin.
task.modelAnswer:
Kuzguncuk: Istanbul's Hidden Village

Kuzguncuk is a small neighbourhood on the Asian side of Istanbul which feels like a village. It's a peaceful place where old wooden houses stand next to each other on narrow streets.

The heart of the neighbourhood is the main street, where you can find little cafés, a bakery and a bookshop whose owner always recommends great novels. On Sundays, the street is lively but never too crowded.

What I love most are the people who live there. Neighbours still say hello to each other and chat outside their doors. It's the kind of place that reminds me of the Istanbul my grandparents talked about.

If you go there, don't miss the small garden by the sea, which is perfect for a cup of tea at sunset. It's definitely worth visiting!

questions.modelAnswer: The person who has influenced me most is my grandmother, Saniye. She's a woman who has always worked hard and never complains. She lives in a small village near Bolu, where she has a garden that's full of fruit trees. When I was a child, I spent every summer there. The house where she lives is more than a hundred years old, and the kitchen is the room I remember best. That's the place where she taught me to make bread. She has a neighbour, Hasan Amca, whose stories made us laugh every evening. The food she cooks still tastes better than anything I've eaten in restaurants. She's the kind of person who makes everyone feel at home.
